articles.title: Oklahoma stun No 1 Texas as Sandell’s last-second kick seals Red River upset
articles.summary: Sandell’s 47-yard kick seals 27-24 upset in Dallas. Sooners overcome offensive struggles to stun Texas. Manning throws three TDs but two costly picks. Tate Sandell kicked a 47-yard field goal on the final play and Oklahoma overcame their continued offensive ineptness with touchdowns on special…
body: The Sooners (3-2, 1-1 Southeastern Conference) beat a No 1 team for the first time since a 38-17 win over Missouri in 2007. They had been 0-4-1 when facing a top-ranked Texas team.
Arch Manning threw three touchdowns for the Longhorns (4-1, 1-1), but both of his interceptions were costly.

Texas had two late chances, but Gianni Spetic was wide right on a 53-yard field-goal attempt with 1:55 left. After the Sooners went three-and-out for the seventh time in the game, Manning’s last pass was intercepted by Courtland Guillory with 19 seconds left.
That set up the Sooners at their 39, and John Mateer completed passes of 13 and 20 yards to Isaiah Sategna on opposite sides of the field, both upheld on replay review.

articles.title: Real Madrid’s Vinícius Júnior sent off for hair-pulling in victory over Villarreal
articles.summary: Yan Diomandé earned Real Madrid a tight 1-0 victory over Villarreal to keep them six points behind La Liga leaders Barcelona, even though winger Vinícius Júnior was sent off for hair pulling.
body: Vinícius, on as a substitute, scored but his goal was disallowed and then he was dismissed after a VAR review showed he had pulled the hair of Villarreal’s Nathan Saliba.

José Mourinho’s side battled through the final stages with 10 men, holding on to win and provisionally going third. But the red card left a bitter taste for Real, with Vinícius running the risk of a potential ban which could keep him out of El Clásico on 25 October.
“I don’t know what’s going on with the referees, with this red card, I don’t understand,” said the Madrid midfielder Aurélien Tchouaméni. “But the most important thing is the victory.”

Kylian Mbappé was fit to start the match for Madrid after suffering a knee problem playing for France during the international break. There were a smattering of whistles for the superstar forward, with some fans believing he has been unprofessional in recent weeks, but also applause from others.

articles.title: USWNT exposed by ruthless Spain as early goals settle heavyweight friendly
articles.summary: Guijarro and Navarro score in opening 14 minutes. US midfield and defensive lapses exposed by Spain. Yohannes misses penalty as US fightback falls short. In less than a year’s time, the United States and Spain will almost certainly arrive in Brazil as the top two contenders to win the Women’s World…
body: This month’s pair of friendlies between the two sides are taking place with caveats. Both sides are missing several of their most important players to injuries. The opening match in Brazil is 258 days away. Spain have booked their place, but the US still have to actually qualify for the World Cup, through a regional tournament that begins next month.

Even without full-strength rosters, a meeting between these two teams is a compelling bill. And in their first of two friendlies, on Saturday in Washington DC, Spain had the upper hand, scoring twice in the first 14 minutes of a 2-0 win.
“You can’t afford to go 2-0 down against the best team in the world, especially the way we conceded those goals,” US coach Emma Hayes said. “That’s the learning.”

In just the fifth meeting between the two sides and the first since 11 October 2022 – before Spain broke through to win the 2023 World Cup – the reigning champions took advantage of defensive lapses and the US midfield’s struggles. After trailing by two goals for the first time under Emma Hayes, the Americans played a much-improved second half, but failures to convert chances and a stopped penalty kept them scoreless.

articles.title: Grambling beats Jackson State 38-34 in offensive showcase
articles.summary: Grambling beats Jackson State 38-34 in offensive showcase appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here. Jackson State has arguably emerged as the best team in HBCU football.
body: Grambling extended its win streak over Jackson State, beating them 45-38 in an offensive showcase. That made it arguably the most exciting game of the weekend in HBCU football. Jackson State jumped out to an early 14-0 lead in the first quarter before Grambling answered with a 5-yard touchdown pass from Jacobe Robinson to Tyson George.

Li’Darius Pryor then ran for a 16-yard gain to put Jackson State up 21-7. Grambling dominated the rest of the second quarter, scoring two straight touchdowns to tie the game 21-21 heading into halftime. Grambling then took the lead in the third quarter when Robinson found Patrick Williams II for a 9-yard touchdown, going up 28-24 after the PAT. Early in the fourth quarter, Grambling padded their lead when Robinson found Landavis Murphy for a 54-yard touchdown reception, putting them up 35-24. But Jackson State wasn’t finished fighting.

articles.title: Steelers Bring Back Doneiko Slaughter Amid Secondary Chaos
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers made a bold move on Saturday afternoon by bringing cornerback Doneiko Slaughter back to the 53-man roster. This isn’t just a routine swap. It is a clear sign that the team is scrambling for help in a secondary that has seen too many bodies get knocked out.
body: After a week of waivers and practice squad shuffling, the front office decided to trust a familiar face who knows the system inside out. The team announced the signing Saturday afternoon, per Behind the Steel Curtain.

Slaughter’s path to this spot has been anything but smooth. He started the season on the practice squad, then got elevated for the first three games. He was signed to the main roster for Week 4, only to be cut and sent back down just days before Week 5.

The back-and-forth nature of his 2026 season shows how thin the depth chart really is. According to Steelers Now, he was released on Monday, cleared waivers on Tuesday, and landed back on the practice squad by Wednesday. That kind of volatility usually spells trouble for a unit trying to find rhythm.

Despite the roster drama, Slaughter has been busy on the field. He has played 52 snaps over the first four games, all while working on the punt return unit. He even recorded two tackles in Week 3 against the Cincinnati Bengals.

articles.title: Ulster playing games like they're training sessions - Murphy
articles.summary: Head coach Richie Murphy says UIster are "playing matches like training sessions" as he expresses his disappointment after Saturday's 26-26 draw with Munster in Belfast.
body: Trailing by 21 points at the break, Ulster hit back as Jacob Stockdale scored his second try of the game before David McCann and Stuart McCloskey struck to earn a second successive United Rugby Championship draw.
Having opened the campaign with a home defeat by Edinburgh and a 33-33 draw in Glasgow, Murphy's side remain winless on the domestic front before starting their European campaign next week.
"We're still very much in the early part of the season. We've got three our four players coming back in for their first games this weekend," said Murphy.
"The flow of the team hasn't completely settled in. At the moment, we're playing matches like they're training sessions.

articles.title: Detroit Red Wings rediscover defense in SO loss to Canadiens
articles.summary: Detroit Red Wings score: Dylan Larkin felt the love from Montreal fans, but the Wings couldn't find the net in a shootout shutout by the Canadiens.
body: MONTREAL – A marathon evening at Bell Centre had fans chanting for Dylan Larkin to join their team, and thwarted for would-be goal celebrations three times.

'We want Lar-kin!" they intoned, on and off, as the Detroit Red Wings faced the Montreal Canadiens for the first time this season, on Saturday, Oct. 10. It was the Wings' second game in two days, their first of the season on the road, against a team that, like the Wings, had only won once in its first four outings.
For the Wings, that still holds, but at least they got a point, falling, 1-0 after a shootout that lasted six rounds.

The game took nearly three hours and was a memorable one. Daniil Tarasov looked good in net in his first start of the season for the Wings (1-3-1), coming through when teammates turned the puck over and got caught in their own zone for stretches. But it wasn't a tilted arena: The Wings tested Jacob Fowler, too, including on an Andrew Copp breakaway early in the third period.

articles.title: Hononegah scores last second touchdown to upset Antioch in Sectional Semi-Finals
articles.summary: ANTIOCH, Ill (WTVO/WQRF) — The Hononegah Indians Girls flag football team has extended their season just a bit longer. They defeated the Antioch Sequoits 13 to 12 at Antioch High School for the Antioch Sectional.
body: Antioch jumped to an early 12 to nothing lead before Hononegah had a chance to respond. Then Hononegah's Layla Demke connected deep with Emma Bullard to help Hononegah score before the Half.
In the second half, it was all defense, with Hononegah's Taitum Cates being credited with multiple sacks on Antioch QB Tanner Ludwig.

With 1:24 remaining in the game, Hononegah had one last chance to hopefully get the win. Demke connected once again with Bullard to get the Indians to the 20-yard line. Then, with around 10 seconds remaining, Demke connected with Claire Vanschelven in the corner of the end zone for the game-winning touchdown.
Hononegah will face off against Crystal Lake Central in the Sectional Championship at Antioch High School on Tuesday, October 13th at 5 pm.

articles.title: Boos, anguish & fading belief -'worrying day' for under-pressure Carrick
articles.summary: It couldn't happen again could it? Another failure to beat 10 men increases pressure on Man Utd boss Michael Carrick after a 1-1 draw against Tottenham Hotspur.
body: For the second time in successive home Premier League games, Manchester United failed to beat opponents reduced to 10 men.
For the third time in as many seasons, a United manager finds himself under severe pressure before the clocks have gone back.

Four weeks ago, Manchester City needed an incorrect video assistant referee (VAR) decision to take advantage of an ineffective United performance after Phil Foden had been shown a red card in the 23rd minute for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes.

On Saturday, the damage was self-inflicted as a Spurs side, who had given every indication of being unable to score before Rodrigo Bentancur's headfirst charge at Luke Shaw just five minutes after Bryan Mbeumo's opener, came up with an injury-time equaliser.

articles.title: Carrick must share burden of Man Utd's underperformance with his players
articles.summary: "We couldn't find a way to get ourselves into the game. With the ball, without the ball, we were off it." A fair assessment from Michael Carrick, if not a wholly explanatory one.
body: Stuck in the mire of Manchester United's worst start to a league season for 40 years, the manager appeared lost for legitimate reasons. His margin for error is shrinking by the week.
Why were his side outplayed at home by the Premier League's bottom club? Why can't they hold onto leads? Why do they seem incapable of playing against 10 men?

All of these are fair questions to put to the man himself and many were asked of Carrick in the wake of Saturday's 1-1 draw with Spurs. None were answered with enough detail to satisfy, though, only really serving to hold a mirror up to what was delivered on the pitch: inadequacy.

Clearly the manager can only accept so much of the blame. His players are yet to offer a single complete performance, only bit-part displays of individualism and self-direction. Where is the cohesiveness that shaped the backend of last year? What happened to the clarity that turned a collapsed season into a third-place finish?

articles.title: A loss to rival Oklahoma hurts, but it will take a lot more to derail Texas' College Football Playoff path
articles.summary: A marquee win over Ohio State and a grueling SEC schedule give the Longhorns enough resume power to potentially crash the 12-team field with three losses
body: But if there's a redeeming thought for Texas fans to cling to amidst the agony of a loss to Oklahoma that never should have happened, it's this: the Longhorns still have margin for error in their quest to reach the College Football Playoff.

The CBS Sports College Football Playoff Forecaster projects Texas with a 66.8% chance to reach the CFP, even after losing to the Sooners. That's because the Longhorns will still have a case for at-large inclusion even if they arrive at Selection Sunday with three losses, which is a distinct possibility.
While the admission of a three-loss team would be a first in the 12-team playoff era, Texas would be a likely candidate to set the precedent if it winds up going 9-3.

Four of Texas' next five games are against opponents who will be ranked in the Week 7 AP poll. Six of the Longhorns' final seven contests are against teams that have been ranked among the top 16 at some point this season. If Texas doesn't get more buttoned up soon, Saturday's defeat won't be its last.
